paper_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the tri-DPP molecule 5b-based solar cell, and what processing conditions were used to achieve it?
qa_pairs.answer: The tri-DPP molecule 5b achieved a peak PCE of 5.5%. This was obtained using a 5b:PC71BM blend ratio of 40:60, processed with 1% 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) as a solvent additive. The device also exhibited a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 10.40 mA/cm², a Voc of 0.86 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 61.7%.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How does the side-chain structure of tri-DPP molecules 5a and 5b affect their solubility in chloroform and their thermal transition temperatures?
qa_pairs.answer: Side-chain branching significantly impacts these properties: molecule 5a, which has branched 2-ethylhexyl chains, shows high solubility (over 25 mg/mL) but lower thermal transitions (Tm of 228 °C and Tc of 196 °C). In contrast, molecule 5b, featuring linear n-hexyl chains, has lower solubility (10 mg/mL) but higher thermal stability with a Tm of 254 °C and a Tc of 234 °C.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What is the structural rationale for the low-lying HOMO energy levels observed in tri-DPP molecules 5a and 5b?
qa_pairs.answer: The low-lying HOMO energy levels (-5.4 eV for 5a and -5.2 eV for 5b) are attributed to the incorporation of an additional electron-deficient diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP) unit into the central position of the molecular backbone. This design results in deeper HOMO levels than those found in most reported DPP-containing polymers and small molecules.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Compare the fill factor (FF) performance of tri-DPP molecules to typical mono-DPP molecules and explain the significance of this comparison.
qa_pairs.answer: Tri-DPP molecules exhibit fill factors exceeding 60%, which is significantly higher than the typical FFs of less than 50% found in mono-DPP compounds. This performance is significant because it makes the tri-DPP molecular systems comparable to polymer-based bulk heterojunction (BHJ) solar cells in terms of charge transport and device physics.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: How do the solvent additive requirements differ between the tri-DPP molecules 5a and 5b during device fabrication?
qa_pairs.answer: Despite their subtle structural differences, the two molecules require different additives for optimal performance: 5a:PC71BM blends require 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO), while 5b:PC71BM blends perform optimally when processed with 1-chloronaphthalene (CN).
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: What evidence from X-ray diffraction (XRD) suggests a difference in the self-assembly of tri-DPP molecules 5a and 5b?
qa_pairs.answer: Thin-film XRD shows that the linear-chain molecule 5b has a much higher tendency for crystallization, evidenced by distinct diffraction peaks with a d-spacing of 1.53 nm in both as-cast and annealed films. The branched-chain molecule 5a, however, only shows a weak diffraction peak at a similar 2θ value after thermal annealing, indicating lower crystallinity.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Describe the charge transport characteristics of 5a and 5b and the effect of thermal annealing on their hole mobility.
qa_pairs.answer: Both molecules exhibit ambipolar charge transport with hole-dominant (p-type) behavior. 5b shows higher hole mobility than 5a; after thermal annealing at 100 °C, the hole mobility increases to maximum values of 4.3 x 10⁻³ cm²/V·s for 5b and 6.1 x 10⁻⁴ cm²/V·s for 5a.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells

qa_pairs.question: Why is the optimized donor-to-acceptor (D:A) ratio of 40:60 for 5b:PC71BM solar cells considered unusual for small-molecule systems?
qa_pairs.answer: A 40:60 D:A ratio reflects a higher acceptor content, which is a characteristic typically observed in polymer-based bulk heterojunction solar cells. In contrast, most high-performance solution-processed small-molecule solar cells are usually optimized at higher donor contents.
qa_pairs.source_title: Tri-Diketopyrrolopyrrole Molecular Donor Materials for High-Performance Solution-Processed Bulk Heterojunction Solar Cells
